candidate.purpose: Stateful stream-processing/dataflow framework that can inform TAGX event-time orchestration, per-symbol state, windowing and recovery semantics.
candidate.latencySuitability: MEDIUM-HIGH for stateful orchestration/windowing; not itself a market-data source and adds a Rust/Python runtime layer.
candidate.maintenance: Community-maintained since May 2025; original company/core team stepped back. Latest reviewed commits include Python 3.13/3.14 support merged 2026-06-20, so maintenance is alive but materially thinner than a fully staffed vendor-backed project.
candidate.docsTests: README documents TestingSource/integration testing, stateful operators, event-time windows, joins, Kafka/custom connectors and recovery; CI badge is present. No claim of TAGX-specific latency has been established.
candidate.securityNotes: No trading credentials required by the engine itself. Direct adoption expands supply-chain/runtime surface through Python + Rust and optional connectors/Kubernetes; custom WebSocket connectors would still need credential isolation and reconnect/freshness tests.
candidate.lookAheadBiasRisk: LOW-MEDIUM if event-time windows and state boundaries are used correctly; unsafe if final labels/outcomes share state with live features.
candidate.integrationPlan: Borrow explicit event-time/session-scoped state and recoverable keyed-state patterns. Do not add Bytewax to production. First benchmark a minimal challenger against TAGX native JSON-state pipeline for restart recovery, session-boundary reset correctness, p95 processing latency and memory.
candidate.reasonNotIntegrated: Community-maintainer risk plus unnecessary runtime complexity for the current GitHub-Actions/JSON hot path; the architecture pattern is useful, the dependency is not yet justified.
